research_question: Does a completed M5 liquidity sweep that rejects a confirmed swing in the direction implied by the latest BOS regime create enough residual 30-second reversal/continuation edge to survive P75 execution?
source_basis: MetaQuotes MQL5 Part 46 defines SwingLength=5, labels HH/HL/LH/LL, sets bullish BOS on HH and bearish BOS on LL.
The source bullish setup requires bullish BOS, prior swing low swept by the completed bar low, close back above that swing low, and close above open; bearish setup mirrors the logic.
TradingView open-source swing-sweep logic independently uses wick beyond a confirmed swing followed by close back inside as a false-break/reclaim event.

frozen_signal.trend_state: latest confirmed higher-high => bullish BOS; latest confirmed lower-low => bearish BOS
frozen_signal.bullish_event: bullish BOS + completed M5 low below current confirmed swing low + close above swing low + close above open
frozen_signal.bearish_event: bearish BOS + completed M5 high above current confirmed swing high + close below swing high + close below open
frozen_signal.direction: BUY bullish SSL reclaim; SELL bearish BSL reclaim
frozen_signal.entry: first executable P75 tick at/after completed sweep-bar right edge

failure_rule: If the single M5 SwingLength=5 source-faithful profile fails supply/day or direct-net gate, retire BOSLS rather than rescue it on Stage-A.
advance_rule: If it passes, freeze unchanged for independent later-January validation.
